The varying widths of the confidence intervals directly reflect the escalating uncertainty as we look further into the future. Outcomes could fall outside these stated intervals due to significant unforeseen events or drastic shifts in fundamental conditions. Conversely, the value could drop below the lower bounds if a severe economic recession or stagflationary environment materializes unexpectedly, if a major geopolitical conflict escalates dramatically, if a significant financial system shock occurs, or if unexpected regulatory crackdowns or policy blunders severely impact market sentiment or specific sectors. These "black swan" or high-impact, low-probability events are inherently difficult to quantify but represent the primary risks to remaining within the forecast ranges.
